name: Kujataa Greenland: Norse and Inuit Farming at the Edge of the Ice Cap
description: In southern Greenland, fjords and green sheep pastures sit beside the ice cap. Norse settlers from Iceland arrived here in the 10th century and brought the Arctic's first farming. Centuries later, Inuit families took up sheep herding in the same valleys. You can still see ruined Norse farmsteads and churches near modern farms, where hunting and grazing continue side by side.
